Revenue Management Services

The revenue management work itself.

This is the hands-on discipline — listings, pricing structure, and market strategy, done by revenue managers. The AI agent monitors the result every single day.

Listing optimisation

Title, description, photo order, amenities and content reviewed and improved, so the listing converts the traffic it already gets.

Listing health checks

A regular audit of each listing against its market: visibility, conversion, review performance and the ranking factors that move it.

PriceLabs setup and management

Full configuration and ongoing management of the pricing engine: base prices, min prices, seasonal profiles, day-of-week adjustments and discounts.

Floor price architecture

A properly calculated minimum for every unit, built from its real cost structure, so no night is ever sold below profitability.

Rate structure and length of stay

Weekday and weekend logic, minimum-stay rules, orphan gap handling and the last-minute strategy that closes the remaining nights.

Seasonal and event strategy

The Dubai calendar priced deliberately: peak season, low season, Eid, DSF, major events and the compression periods around them.

Competitor and tower analysis

The comp set defined properly — including the competitors inside your own building — and then monitored, not set once and forgotten.

Performance review

A monthly review of ADR, occupancy, RevPAR and MPI against the market — with the strategy adjusted from what the result actually says.

Revenue managers do this work. The AI watches it every day. The agent flags what moved overnight; the strategy behind it is set, reviewed and defended by people.

Why This Exists

Most STR operators are flying without instruments.

Problem 01

No floor price discipline

Without a hard minimum, every discount decision erodes margin — and nobody notices until month end.

Problem 02

Static pricing that does not respond

Rates set once and left alone cannot react to demand shifts, events, or booking pace.

Problem 03

Generic automation with no judgment

Without interpretation, automation automates mistakes — at scale, every single day.

Problem 04

Missed event and demand premiums

Event nights and compression windows can carry entire months — and most operators price straight through them.

Problem 05

Slow reaction to demand shifts

72-hour demand surges come and go before anyone checks the data. Those windows are missed revenue.

Problem 06

Occupancy as a proxy for revenue

Full calendars can still lose money. The target is RevPAR, not occupancy.

How this is calculated

Break-even = (fixed cost per occupied night + cleaning ÷ avg stay + other variable cost) ÷ (1 − fees%) — occupied nights per month = 30.4 × expected occupancy.

Hard floor = break-even ÷ 0.90 (10% occupancy-safety buffer) · Last-minute floor = hard floor × 0.85, never below marginal cost · Orphan gap fill = marginal cost × 1.10 — any rate above true variable cost beats an empty night · Weekend floor = hard floor × 1.15 · Low-season base = hard floor × 1.05 · Peak minimum = hard floor × 1.50.

This mirrors the logic of our free Excel tool. Results are estimates for guidance only — not financial advice.

FAQ

Questions we get asked

Everything you need to know before getting started. Still have questions? Talk to us directly on WhatsApp.

How is Oasis Revenue Lab different from just using PriceLabs?

PriceLabs adjusts rates algorithmically, but it cannot tell you whether your strategy is working, whether your floor is correct, or what the market is actually doing. Oasis Revenue Lab sits on top: daily monitoring, market interpretation, floor verification, and clear recommendations. We also configure and manage PriceLabs for you.

Do you change my prices automatically?

Not yet. Today the agent runs in advisory mode — it recommends, you decide. A supervised autopilot is in development in collaboration with PriceLabs, with operator-defined guardrails (your floor, your ceiling, your rules). Existing clients get it first.

What do I need to get started?

An active PriceLabs account and Telegram. We take your listing details and run a short onboarding call to set your floors and goals. Setup takes under 48 hours.

How much does it cost?

AED 80 per listing per month at the founding rate, locked in permanently for the first 20 clients. The standard price rises after launch. Hybrid and consultancy engagements are priced custom to your portfolio.

Do you only cover Dubai?

Currently, yes. Our deepest data covers JBR, Dubai Marina, Downtown, Business Bay, and Palm Jumeirah. GCC expansion is planned for 2026.

I already have a property manager. Does this still work?

Yes — Oasis Revenue Lab works alongside your property manager as the revenue intelligence layer. If your PM handles pricing, we can work with them directly on the strategy layer.

How long until I see results?

Briefings start within 48 hours. Portfolios that are underpriced or missing floor discipline typically improve within 2–4 weeks. Outcomes are tracked via Hostaway.

Is there a contract?

No long-term contract. Service is monthly rolling — cancel with 30 days notice. The founding rate is locked for 18 months for launch-phase clients, and after that it stays at your signed rate.

Do you work with properties outside holiday homes?

Our focus is short-term rentals on Airbnb and Booking.com priced with PriceLabs. Serviced apartments and boutique hotels are on the roadmap.

Who is behind Oasis Revenue Lab?

Oasis Revenue Lab is a division of Lux Oasis Advisory & Services LLC, registered in the Sharjah Free Zone, UAE. Our operating partner is Lux Oasis Holiday Homes, a separate UAE company that holds the DTCM licence — and every system runs on that live portfolio before it reaches a client.

Still have questions? Talk to us directly — every enquiry is handled personally.
